To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) exposure of mice to 2 GHz radiofrequency fields for up to 2 years had no effect on the expression of the water channel AQP‐4 in brain, a protein that is upregulated in response to blood‐brain barrier injury, and (2) the lack of effect on AQP‐4 suggests that exposure to mobile telephone fields does not produce blood‐brain barrier damage.
exposure to mobile phone microradiowaves for a short (1 h) or long (24 months) duration did not cause an increase in the expression of the water channel aquaporin‐ 4 in mouse brains.
exposure of the brain to mobile telephone RF does not cause upregulation of the principal water channel in brain, aquaporin 4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF EMFs), which are emitted from a variety of sources, including mobile phones.
the possible health effects of exposure to mobile telephone microwaves.
the effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic field (RF EMF) on the central nervous system (CNS) and, in particular, on the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of an effect of exposure to mobile phone micropower RF fields on the blood brain barrier.

the exposure of mouse brains to mobile phone RF fields for 2 years does not result in any detectable up‐ regulation of AQP‐ 4 expression, and therefore does not result in a detectable increase in blood–brain barrier permeability.
the present study provides no evidence that mobile telephone microwaves cause an increase in blood‐blood barrier permeability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no convincing evidence that exposure to mobile telephone RF causes any significant increase in BBB permeability.
we found no evidence for a microwave effect on the blood–brain barrier in mice exposed to mobile phone radiation.
we did not find any evidence for an increased blood‐brain barrier (BBB) permeability in mice exposed to mobile phone radiofrequency (RF).
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no evidence that exposure to RF fields from mobile phones or mobile phone base stations increases the permeability of the blood–brain barrier.

we have shown that exposure to RF from mobile phones, either acutely (60 minutes) and long term (104 weeks), does not cause an increase in AQP4, the principal water channel in brain, which is indicative of an increase in blood‐ brain barrier permeability.
there is no detectable effect of mobile phone microwaving of the mouse brain on the expression of the major water channel protein, and therefore on the integrity of the blood–brain barrier.
